records.question: Can my contract stop me from working for a competitor after I leave?
records.text:
Yes, your contract can include a non-compete clause preventing you from working for a competitor after you leave, but only under specific conditions.
First, any clause requiring you to work for the employer for your entire lifetime or to refrain from practicing any trade or profession for your entire lifetime is null and void [labour-2004:43].
Second, a valid non-compete clause is only permitted if the nature of your work allowed you to know the employer's clients or access the establishment's business secrets [labour-2004:43]. In such cases, the employer may stipulate that you shall not compete, participate, or work in any competing project in the same sector after the contract ends [labour-2004:43].
The duration of this non-compete condition must not exceed one year in all cases [labour-2004:43].
The non-compete clause becomes null and void if any of the termination cases specified in Article 51 are fulfilled, or if the employer terminates you in violation of the provisions of Article 61 [labour-2004:43].

verdicts.reason: article states any clause requiring lifetime work or lifetime restraint is null

verdicts.claim: Second, a valid non-compete clause is only permitted if the nature of your work allowed you to know the employer's clients or access the establishment's business secrets.
verdicts.reason: article requires nature of work to allow client or secret knowledge

verdicts.claim: In such cases, the employer may stipulate that you shall not compete, participate, or work in any competing project in the same sector after the contract ends.
verdicts.reason: article allows stipulation of non‑compete after termination

verdicts.reason: article limits duration to one year

records.question: When must my final salary and dues be paid after my contract ends?

However, if the worker leaves the work without giving the notice required by Article 49, the employer must pay the remuneration and all other dues within a period not exceeding seven days from the date of leaving the work [labour-2004:67].

records.question: Where do I file a complaint if I have a dispute with my employer?
records.text:
For an individual dispute regarding the application of the Labour Law or the employment contract, you must refer the dispute to the Department of Labour Relations or the Department of National Human Resources Development at the Ministry, as applicable, for amicable settlement [labour-2004:115-bis].
For a collective labour dispute, the parties must first attempt to settle it between themselves, and if a joint committee exists in the establishment, the dispute must be referred to that committee [labour-2004:129]. If this fails, the workers must submit their complaint in writing to the employer, sending a copy to the Department [labour-2004:129]. If the employer's written reply does not settle the dispute, the Department will attempt to settle it through mediation [labour-2004:129]. If mediation fails within fifteen days of the employer's reply, the Department must refer the dispute to a conciliation committee [labour-2004:130].

records.question: Is my employer allowed to keep my passport?
records.text: No, your employer is not allowed to keep your passport by default. records.question: Is Friday a day off, and what am I paid if I have to work on my rest day?
records.text: Yes, Friday is the usual weekly rest day for all workers, except for shift workers [labour-2004:75]. If you are required to work on your weekly rest day, you must be compensated with another day off and paid either the amount payable for the weekly rest day or your basic wage plus an increment of at least 150% of that basic wage [labour-2004:75].

records.question: ماذا أفعل إذا حدث خلاف بيني وبين صاحب العمل على الراتب؟
records.text:
يجب عليك أولاً محاولة تسوية النزاع ودياً مع صاحب العمل، وإذا وجدت لجنة مشتركة في المنشأة وجب عرض النزاع عليها [labour-2004:129].
وفي حال فشل التسوية الودية، يجب عليك تقديم شكواك أو طلبك كتابةً إلى صاحب العمل مع إرسال نسخة منه إلى الإدارة [labour-2004:129].
يجب على صاحب العمل الرد كتابةً على شكواك خلال أسبوع من تاريخ استلامه لها، مع إرسال نسخة من رده إلى الإدارة [labour-2004:129].
إذا لم يؤدِ رد صاحب العمل إلى تسوية النزاع، تسعى الإدارة لتسويته عن طريق وساطتها [labour-2004:129].
وإذا لم تؤدِ وساطة الإدارة إلى تسوية النزاع خلال خمسة عشر يوماً من تاريخ رد صاحب العمل، تُحال القضية إلى لجنة توفيق [labour-2004:130].
يكون قرار لجنة التوفيق ملزماً لك ولصاحب العمل إذا كنتم قد وافقتم كتابةً على إحالة النزاع إليها قبل اجتماعها، وإلا يُحال النزاع إلى لجنة تحكيم خلال خمسة عشر يوماً ويكون التحكيم إجبارياً على الطرفين [labour-2004:130].

records.question: How many weeks of sick leave are paid, and at what rate?
records.text: A worker is entitled to a total of six weeks of paid sick leave per year of service [labour-2004:82]. The first two weeks are paid at the full wage rate, and the following four weeks are paid at half the wage rate [labour-2004:82]. Any sick leave extending beyond these six weeks is unpaid [labour-2004:82]. The wage used for this calculation is the worker's basic wage on the due date, or the average remuneration for the preceding three months if the worker is on a piecework basis [labour-2004:72].

records.question: Can I be fired while I am on leave?
records.text: No, an employer may not terminate your labour contract or notify you of its termination during any of the leaves stipulated in the law [labour-2004:85]. Additionally, the employer may not notify you of termination if the notice period would end during any of these leaves [labour-2004:85]. records.question: Because the Ramadan limit is 20 working hours a week, can my employer ask me to do more?
records.text:
The sources do not state a 20-hour weekly limit for Ramadan. For adult workers, the maximum ordinary working hours during Ramadan are thirty-six hours per week (six hours per day) [labour-2004:73]. For minors, the limit is twenty-four hours per week (four hours per day) [labour-2004:90].
Regarding whether an employer can ask for more work:
1. **Overtime:** Employers may require additional hours beyond the ordinary limits, provided the total actual working hours do not exceed ten hours per day [labour-2004:74].
2. **Payment:** For these additional hours, the employer must pay at least the basic wage plus an increment of not less than 25% [labour-2004:74]. If the work is performed between 9 pm and 3 am (excluding shift workers), the increment must be at least 50% [labour-2004:74].
3. **Weekly Rest:** If the work necessitates working on the weekly rest day (Friday), the worker must be compensated with another rest day and paid either the wage for the rest day or the basic wage plus an increment of at least 150% [labour-2004:75].
Therefore, while the *ordinary* hours are capped at 36 (adults) or 24 (minors) in Ramadan, an employer can require more hours as overtime, subject to the daily cap of 10 hours and the specified premium pay rates [labour-2004:73][labour-2004:90][labour-2004:74].

verdicts.claim: The sources do not state a 20-hour weekly limit for Ramadan.
verdicts.reason: Article 73 states 36 hours in Ramadan, no 20-hour limit.

verdicts.reason: Article 73 specifies 36 hours/week, 6h/day in Ramadan.

verdicts.claim: For minors, the limit is twenty-four hours per week (four hours per day).
verdicts.reason: Article 90 specifies 24 hours/week, 4h/day for minors in Ramadan.

verdicts.claim: **Overtime:** Employers may require additional hours beyond the ordinary limits, provided the total actual working hours do not exceed ten hours per day.
verdicts.reason: Article 74 allows overtime up to 10h/day.

verdicts.claim: **Payment:** For these additional hours, the employer must pay at least the basic wage plus an increment of not less than 25%.
verdicts.reason: Article 74 requires at least 25% premium on basic wage for overtime.

verdicts.claim: If the work is performed between 9 pm and 3 am (excluding shift workers), the increment must be at least 50%.
verdicts.reason: Article 74 states 50% premium for 9pm-3am (excluding shift workers).

verdicts.claim: **Weekly Rest:** If the work necessitates working on the weekly rest day (Friday), the worker must be compensated with another rest day and paid either the wage for the rest day or the basic wage plus an increment of at least 150%.
verdicts.reason: Article 75 requires alternate rest day and 150% premium for work on Friday.

verdicts.claim: Therefore, while the *ordinary* hours are capped at 36 (adults) or 24 (minors) in Ramadan, an employer can require more hours as overtime, subject to the daily cap of 10 hours and the specified premium pay rates.
